name: Zadar Airport
before:
Zadar's airport, at Zemunik Donji 8 km from the city centre, and fourth busiest in Croatia with around 1.6 million passengers in 2025 across more than 70 destinations.

It is the only airport in the country with two runways, and it doubles as the Croatian Air Force's main training base.

Low cost carriers made it what it is. Ryanair based a 737 here in April 2013 and Lauda followed with A320s and a long list of new routes, so summer capacity is much larger than the winter timetable suggests.

There is a good story attached to the site. For years it was one of the very few airports anywhere where the taxiway crossed a public road. The road was closed in April 2010 under terms negotiated during Croatia's European Union accession, and in 2020 an underpass was built so it could reopen.

Zadar has had commercial flights since 1936, when the city was part of the Italian province of Zara.
after:
Zadar's airport sits at Zemunik Donji, about 10 km east of the city centre. It was Croatia's fourth busiest in 2025, with around 1.6 million passengers.

Of Croatia's airports with scheduled flights, it is the only one with two runways.

Low cost carriers made it what it is, and Ryanair has a base here. The airport's own figures show how seasonal the traffic is: 364,473 passengers in August 2025 against 1,808 in January.

claims.inAfter: about 10 km east of the city centre.
claims.note: Was '8 km from the city centre' (Wikipedia; the operator's own page says Zadar is 7 km away), which fails the coordinates check: the airport is 10.5 km in a straight line from the GeoNames centre of Zadar, at 101 degrees, and a road cannot be shorter than the straight line. Two independent position sets agree on about 10 km: OurAirports' airport with GeoNames' centre (10.5 km), and Ryanair's own airport position (44.1083, 15.3467) with Wikipedia's coordinates for Zadar (44.1142, 15.2275), which are 9.5 km apart at about 94 degrees, also east. The 7 and 8 km figures probably measure to the edge of the city; with no source saying so, neither is used.
